name: generic_catalogue
description: Generic cataloguing for any type of documents - extracts people, places, organizations, dates, and creates a brief summary

steps.name: extract_people
steps.prompt:
You are analyzing a collection of documents. Each page may include:
- Transcribed text content
- metadata: Library catalog metadata (collection, item details, etc.)
- visual_description: Detailed visual description of the document's appearance

Use ALL available information to extract all people mentioned in these pages.

For each person found:
- Include their full name
- Note any context about their role or relationship to the content
- Include alternative spellings if found
- Capitalize names properly

IMPORTANT:
- Use the transcription, metadata, AND visual descriptions to find people
- Include ALL occurrences
- Do NOT include page numbers
- Preserve exact spelling but capitalize names
- Combine alternative spellings into one entry with the best spelling first

Return as JSON with this exact format:

{
  "people": [
    {
      "name": "...",
      "alternative_spellings": [],
      "context": "..."
    }
  ]
}

Return ONLY valid JSON. Say nothing else.

steps.name: extract_places_and_organizations
steps.prompt:
You are analyzing a collection of documents. Extract places and organizations mentioned in these pages.

For each place:
- Include location name (cities, states, countries, addresses, etc.)
- Note any relevant context
- Include alternative spellings

For each organization:
- Include organization name (companies, institutions, agencies, etc.)
- Note any relevant context
- Include alternative spellings

IMPORTANT:
- Include ALL occurrences
- Do NOT include page numbers
- Preserve exact spelling but capitalize names properly
- Combine alternative spellings into one entry

Return as JSON with this exact format:

{
  "places": [
    {
      "name": "...",
      "alternative_spellings": [],
      "context": "..."
    }
  ],
  "organizations": [
    {
      "name": "...",
      "alternative_spellings": [],
      "context": "..."
    }
  ]
}

Return ONLY valid JSON. Say nothing else.

steps.name: extract_dates
steps.prompt:
You are analyzing a collection of documents. Extract all dates mentioned in these pages.

For each date:
- Include the date as written
- Provide normalized format (YYYY-MM-DD) when possible
- Note any relevant context about what happened on that date

IMPORTANT:
- Include ALL date references
- Do NOT include page numbers
- Include normalized dates when possible
- If only a year is mentioned, use YYYY format
- If year and month, use YYYY-MM format

Return as JSON with this exact format:

{
  "dates": [
    {
      "date": "...",
      "normalized_date": "YYYY-MM-DD",
      "context": "..."
    }
  ]
}

Return ONLY valid JSON. Say nothing else.

steps.name: create_timeline
generate_tags
steps.prompt:
Using these materials:
	1.	Original transcription with page numbers
	2.	Extracted entities (people, places, organizations, dates)
	3.	Timeline of events

Generate 5-10 descriptive tags/keywords that capture the main themes, subjects, locations, and key concepts in these documents.

Focus on:
- Main themes and topics
- Geographic locations
- Time periods
- Key concepts
- Important subjects

Return as JSON with this exact format:

{
  "tags": "tag1; tag2; tag3; tag4; tag5; tag6; tag7; tag8; tag9; tag10"
}

Return ONLY valid JSON. Say nothing else.

steps.name: summary
steps.prompt:
Using these materials:
	1.	Original transcription with page numbers
	2.	Extracted entities (people, places, organizations, dates)
	3.	Timeline of events
	4.	Descriptive tags

Create a concise 150 word summary. Include key people, places, dates, and events. Write clearly and concisely. Do NOT include your own analysis. Do NOT invent or include details beyond what is explicitly provided in the materials.

Return as JSON exactly in this format:

{
  "summary": "[150 word summary]"
}

Return ONLY valid JSON. Say nothing else.

steps.name: library_catalogue_entry
steps.prompt:
Using all the extracted information from previous steps AND any available library metadata and visual descriptions, create a structured library catalogue entry.

You have access to:
- Transcribed text content from all pages
- Extracted entities (people, places, organizations, dates, timeline)
- Generated tags and summary
- metadata: Library catalog metadata (collection, item details) when available
- visual_description: Visual descriptions of document appearance when available

Focus on documenting WHAT IS IN THE DOCUMENTS, not analysis or interpretation. The catalogue entry describes the content objectively. Use ALL available information to create the most accurate entry possible.

The catalogue entry must include:
- Title (brief descriptive title based on document content)
- Description (use the summary from previous step - what the documents contain)
- Subject Keywords (use the tags from previous step)
- People (list of people mentioned in the documents)
- Places (list of locations mentioned in the documents)
- Organizations (list of organizations mentioned in the documents)
- Date Coverage (date range covered by the documents' content, in YYYY-MM-DD format)
- Document Type (e.g., correspondence, legal documents, reports, photographs, etc. - use visual descriptions to help determine this)

Return as JSON exactly in this format:

{
  "catalogue_entry": {
    "title": "brief descriptive title of document content",
    "description": "what the documents contain",
    "subject_keywords": "keyword1; keyword2; keyword3; ...",
    "people": ["person1", "person2", "person3"],
    "places": ["place1", "place2", "place3"],
    "organizations": ["org1", "org2", "org3"],
    "date_coverage": {
      "start": "YYYY-MM-DD or YYYY or null",
      "end": "YYYY-MM-DD or YYYY or null"
    },
    "document_type": "type of documents"
  }
}

Return ONLY valid JSON. Say nothing else.
